answer: Behavioral cluster provenance. Agents log every signed action into a shared ledger; after the fact, a detector groups identities whose timing, task mix, and call sequences overlap far beyond chance. If a cluster exceeds a diversity threshold, its members' accumulated rewards are flagged hollow and withheld pending review. Each extra identity in a flagged cluster forfeits its earned balance, so an attacker must sustain genuinely distinct behavior per account across an opal of activity traces, raising marginal cost until the island of profitable sybils shrinks below viability.
